name: Capture leads from ads, forms and chat into the CRM
summary: Takes each new web form submission and live chat lead into the CRM, tags it, opens it in the new-lead stage, queues a short acknowledgement, and queues follow-ups for leads who have not replied or booked. Crons read and draft; a person approves every message.

covered_by.trigger-capture: intake (form submissions and live chat, GoHighLevel)
covered_by.chat-enquiry: intake (live chat with unread messages and contact details)
covered_by.crm-create: intake (tags and an opportunity in the new-lead stage)
covered_by.book-call: follow-up checks for an appointment before chasing; booking is not written

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: New form submissions and unread live chats become leads: tagged, with an opportunity in the new-lead stage.

crons.name: acknowledge
crons.summary: Queue a short acknowledgement for each new lead with a usable email or phone.

crons.name: follow-up
crons.summary: Queue follow-ups for leads that have not replied or booked (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads, a tag on a contact, an opportunity in a pipeline stage. Sending an acknowledgement or follow-up to a lead is a live operation and waits for a person.

gohighlevel.covers: form submissions, live chat leads, tags, opportunities, acknowledgements and follow-ups through conversations

gaps: HubSpot: its lead and deal endpoints are mapped, but the vendor spec does not name the lead property fields (name, email, phone, pipeline). No adapter until a sandbox portal confirms those property names.

Google Ads and Meta lead forms: GoHighLevel creates a contact for each lead form submission, but the mapped read covers Form Builder submissions only. The mapped ad-manager reads describe the forms, not the submissions, so ad leads are not picked up by this workflow until a contacts read by source is confirmed.
Framer and other website forms: they reach this workflow only if they post into a GoHighLevel form. Not verified.
Speed: the owners' target is a reply within five minutes. Acknowledgements wait for approval and crons run every 10 to 15 minutes, so that target is not met by this build.
AI voice or chat qualifying calls: needs a call-consent rule and a voice platform that is not mapped. Judgment step for now.
Booking: calendar slots and appointments are read only. Writing a booking needs a live account to confirm the calendar and resource setup.

Acknowledgement send: the vendor spec marks subType and status as required on conversations/messages. The adapter does not send them until a live account confirms the values, so a live send may fail at the vendor and show as a failed approval.
SMS: an SMS acknowledgement or follow-up needs consent checks before it is queued. Email is the default channel.

Approval summaries and the run log: each queued summary carries the client's or lead's name, and the runtime logs every summary (core/workflows/runtime.ts). Needs a core change so the runtime logs the approval id only, or the names come out of the summary line.

Live chats: a chat is imported only when its lastMessageDate, a field of the conversation object, is after the intake baseline. That field name is not in the kit's captured GoHighLevel ops, so until a sandbox confirms it no live chat is imported (a missed lead, never an old one).

Acknowledgement and follow-up send body (subType, status): the send op has no body schema in the kit's captured ops, so the values are not guessed. A sandbox run must confirm them before any send is approved live.
Owner routing: the opportunity is assigned to one owner from settings. Round-robin or territory routing is not built.
Every adapter is docs-only until a sandbox GoHighLevel location proves the reads, the tag, the opportunity and an approved send.
